subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Coffee Leaf Rust: An Economic Plague
description: A micro-lesson that makes Coffee Leaf Rust: An Economic Plague usable.

hook.text: Coffee leaf rust is a fungus that destroyed 70% of Central America's crop in 2012. It nearly bankrupted nations.

buildup.text: The fungus, Hemileia vastatrix, attacks leaves, stopping photosynthesis. Trees weaken and stop producing cherries.

discovery.text: In the 1800s, rust wiped out Sri Lanka's coffee industry entirely—the country switched to growing tea instead.

twist.text: Climate change is making rust worse. Warmer temperatures let the fungus spread to higher altitudes it couldn't reach before.

climax.text: Rust-resistant varieties exist but taste worse. The industry races to breed plants that are both resistant and delicious.

punchline.text: A fungus reshaped nations and still threatens the industry today.

quiz.question: What happened to Sri Lanka's coffee industry due to leaf rust?
options: It was wiped out—the country switched to tea

details.summary: Coffee leaf rust, caused by the fungus Hemileia vastatrix, devastated Central American coffee production in 2012 and has caused crises throughout coffee history. It kills leaves, destroys yields, and can wipe out entire farms. Warming temperatures are expanding its range to higher altitudes.
details.whyItMatters: Leaf rust is coffee's most destructive disease. It has reshaped the map of coffee production before and threatens to do so again as climate change shifts growing regions.
takeaways: Coffee leaf rust is caused by the fungus Hemileia vastatrix
The 2012 outbreak devastated Central American production
Climate change is pushing rust to previously safe altitudes

faq.question: How does coffee leaf rust spread?
faq.answer: Rust spores travel by wind, rain splash, and on workers' clothing. Warm, humid conditions accelerate spread. Once spores land on a leaf, they germinate and create orange-yellow lesions that destroy the leaf's ability to photosynthesize. Severe infections defoliate and kill trees.

faq.question: Can coffee leaf rust be cured or prevented?
faq.answer: Fungicides can slow outbreaks but are expensive and must be applied preventively. Resistant varieties like Castillo and Catimor carry robusta genes that confer partial immunity. Shade management and good nutrition also help trees resist infection, but no solution is permanent.
